function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check a reputable financial news or market‑data website that updates continuously, such as:

| Source | Typical update frequency | How to find the price |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Every few seconds | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” on Bloomberg.com or the Bloomberg terminal |
| **Kitco** | Every minute | Visit kitco.com/price-charts/ |
| **Reuters** | Every few seconds | Search “Gold” on Reuters.com |
| **Investing.com** | Every minute | Look up “Gold” under commodities |
| **Yahoo Finance** | Every minute | Search “Gold” or ticker “XAUUSD” |

If you need the price for a specific time (e.g., 10:00 AM ET), you can usually find a historical chart that shows the price at each minute.  For the most accurate and up‑to‑date figure, use one of the sites above or your brokerage’s market data feed.
